input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.
The issue is happening on my phone with the number 555-123-2002. That’s the only line I’m using right now.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. What should I do next?
Looking at my status bar, I see that Airplane Mode is turned on. What should I do next?
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see a signal bar with “Poor” signal, it says 2G, and it looks like mobile data is disabled. What should I do next?
I’ve enabled mobile data. The status bar still shows a poor signal and 2G. What should I do next to change the network mode?
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows an excellent signal, 5G, and mobile data is enabled. Should I try the speed test again?
I ran the speed test again, but it still failed and says there’s no connection, even though I have an excellent 5G signal and data is enabled. What should I try next?
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I don’t see any errors or blank fields. What should I do next?
I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but the speed test still fails and says there’s no connection. Is there anything else I can try? I really need to get excellent internet speed.

If there’s nothing else I can try on my end, yes, please transfer me to a technical support agent. I really need to get this fixed so I can have excellent internet speed on my phone. Thank you for your help so far!

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and help troubleshoot your mobile data problem.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.

Thank you for providing your information. To help resolve your mobile data issue, could you please confirm which phone number (or line) you are experiencing the slow or non-working data on? You may have multiple lines on your account, so specifying the affected number will help me assist you more efficiently.
The issue is happening on my phone with the number 555-123-2002. That’s the only line I’m using right now.

Thank you for confirming. To troubleshoot your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a quick speed test on your phone. This will help determine if your data connection is active and what speed you’re currently getting.

Could you please run a speed test on your device and let me know the result? If you need instructions on how to do this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since the speed test failed and reported no connection, let’s check a few things on your device to diagnose the issue:

1. Is Airplane Mode turned ON?
2. Is your SIM card properly inserted and active?
3. Are your mobile data settings enabled?

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see an airplane icon,
- If there are any signal bars,
- If you see a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, 5G, etc.), or if it says “No Service” or “No Signal”.

This information will help me guide you through the next steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Looking at my status bar, I see that Airplane Mode is turned on. What should I do next?

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. This will re-enable all wireless connections, including your mobile data. 

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your mobile data connection returns and try running the speed test again. Let me know if you see your signal bars and a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, or 5G) after turning off Airplane Mode, or if you still have issues.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see a signal bar with “Poor” signal, it says 2G, and it looks like mobile data is disabled. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Here’s what we should do next:

1. Enable mobile data on your phone.
2. Change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G, since 2G is very slow and not suitable for modern internet use.

Please enable mobile data first. Once you’ve done that, let me know, and I’ll guide you through changing your network mode to improve your speed.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
I’ve enabled mobile data. The status bar still shows a poor signal and 2G. What should I do next to change the network mode?

To improve your speed, you should change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G. Please go to your phone’s network settings and select the option for “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G preferred” (the exact wording may vary depending on your device).

Once you’ve changed the network mode, check your status bar again to see if it now shows 4G, LTE, or 5G, and if your signal improves. Let me know what you see after making this change, or if you need help finding the setting on your device.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows an excellent signal, 5G, and mobile data is enabled. Should I try the speed test again?

Yes, please run the speed test again now that your phone is showing an excellent signal and 5G with mobile data enabled. Let me know the result of the speed test and if your internet speed has improved.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I ran the speed test again, but it still failed and says there’s no connection, even though I have an excellent 5G signal and data is enabled. What should I try next?

Since you have an excellent 5G signal and mobile data is enabled, but the speed test still fails, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the internet, even if you have a strong signal.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if you see any errors or if the APN/MMSC fields are blank or incorrect. If you’re unsure how to check this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the process.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I don’t see any errors or blank fields. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since your APN and MMSC settings appear correct and you still have no data connection, let’s try resetting your APN settings to default. Sometimes, even if the fields look correct, a reset can resolve hidden configuration issues.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Let me know once you have reset the APN settings and rebooted your phone, and then try the speed test again. If you need instructions on how to reset APN settings or reboot your device, let me know your phone type.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
